transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` argument and naming the return.

Attached the generated mutable prefix/final-frame postconditions directly to the executable target: the `N <= old(slice)@.len()` Some branch, returned-prefix array view, final slice replacement by `*final(ret.unwrap())`, and the too-short None branch frame preservation.

Preserved the Rust 1.96 branch flow: `if self.len() < N { None } else { Some(unsafe { &mut *(self.as_mut_ptr().cast_array()) }) }`; the implicit receiver and chained raw-pointer operations are the only Verus syntax adaptations.

Reused the reviewed `core::slice::as_mut_ptr` dependency shape through a local executable `as_mut_ptr` wrapper with `slice_start_mut_ptr` and final-frame preservation, and isolated only Verus-unsupported `ptr.cast_array()` plus `unsafe { &mut *ptr }` as named source-backed raw-pointer/provenance and mutable array-reference final-frame boundaries.
